title: Participate in business continuity planning and exercises: decision comparison 1
teachingQuestion: How do business owners turn disruption consequences into continuity priorities, workable alternatives, and evidence from an exercise?
focalInsight: Critical function, BIA, priority, manual workaround, external dependency, communications, and remediation.
caption: Compare meaning, decision conditions, and failures. These concise distinctions are paired with the worked examples in the teaching unit.

nodes.label: Business Continuity
nodes.definition: The organization’s ability and planning discipline to sustain prioritized business functions through disruption and transition to normal operations.
nodes.decision: Frame continuity around essential outcomes, people, facilities, suppliers, data, and communications—not only IT recovery.
nodes.failureExample: Restoring servers while customer support and approvals cannot operate is not business continuity.
nodes.detail: The organization’s ability and planning discipline to sustain prioritized business functions through disruption and transition to normal operations.

nodes.label: Continuity Planning
nodes.definition: The owner-led process of identifying disruption scenarios, priorities, resources, alternatives, roles, and recovery/return criteria.
nodes.decision: Plan with business, facilities, HR, suppliers, and technology owners before an event; revise when their assumptions change.
nodes.failureExample: A technology-only plan may omit staff shortages or contractual dependencies that halt the function.
nodes.detail: The owner-led process of identifying disruption scenarios, priorities, resources, alternatives, roles, and recovery/return criteria.

nodes.label: Critical Function
nodes.definition: A business activity whose unacceptable interruption drives a continuity priority, such as payments, safety response, or regulatory reporting.
nodes.decision: Have the business owner identify the function and consequence; do not infer criticality from system cost or popularity.
nodes.failureExample: Treating a high-cost but deferrable system as first priority can delay a time-sensitive obligation.
nodes.detail: A business activity whose unacceptable interruption drives a continuity priority, such as payments, safety response, or regulatory reporting.

nodes.label: Business Impact Analysis
nodes.definition: A structured assessment of disruption consequences over time that supplies business requirements for continuity and recovery.
nodes.decision: Use business-owner input to determine impacts, tolerances, dependencies, and priority; validate when business conditions change.
nodes.failureExample: An asset inventory cannot reveal the mounting legal or safety consequence of a delayed business process.
nodes.detail: A structured assessment of disruption consequences over time that supplies business requirements for continuity and recovery.

nodes.label: Continuity Priority
nodes.definition: The agreed order in which business functions receive continuity resources based on time-sensitive impact and accepted tolerances.
nodes.decision: Set priority through accountable business decisions informed by BIA, then communicate the tradeoff to resource owners.
nodes.failureExample: Letting the loudest technical owner choose priority can starve a more time-critical function.
nodes.detail: The agreed order in which business functions receive continuity resources based on time-sensitive impact and accepted tolerances.

nodes.label: Manual Workaround
nodes.definition: A predesigned nonstandard way to perform a critical function when normal people, place, process, or technology is unavailable.
nodes.decision: Use when it can safely sustain the function for a defined period; test staffing, records, approvals, and later reconciliation.
nodes.failureExample: Paper orders without later reconciliation can preserve availability while corrupting records.
nodes.detail: A predesigned nonstandard way to perform a critical function when normal people, place, process, or technology is unavailable.

nodes.label: Continuity Exercise
nodes.definition: A planned practice of continuity roles, alternatives, and decisions under a disruption scenario.
nodes.decision: Choose an exercise that tests the business function and its dependencies, not merely technical failover.
nodes.failureExample: A server-failover test that never involves business staff leaves continuity of the customer process unknown.
nodes.detail: A planned practice of continuity roles, alternatives, and decisions under a disruption scenario.

nodes.label: Exercise Scope
nodes.definition: The stated functions, locations, participants, dependencies, scenario, boundaries, and evidence included in a continuity exercise.
nodes.decision: Include the business function’s real dependencies and explicit exclusions so evidence can be interpreted honestly.
nodes.failureExample: Excluding the verification vendor from a payment continuity exercise produces a misleading pass.
nodes.detail: The stated functions, locations, participants, dependencies, scenario, boundaries, and evidence included in a continuity exercise.

nodes.label: Continuity Evidence
nodes.definition: Objective records showing whether the prioritized function, communication, alternative process, and acceptance conditions performed as planned.
nodes.decision: Collect outcomes such as timelines, work products, decision records, reconciliation, and owner acceptance against stated criteria.
nodes.failureExample: Attendance and enthusiastic discussion do not prove the function continued within its tolerance.
nodes.detail: Objective records showing whether the prioritized function, communication, alternative process, and acceptance conditions performed as planned.

learningContract.teachingQuestion: How do business owners turn disruption consequences into continuity priorities, workable alternatives, and evidence from an exercise?
learningContract.misconception: Business continuity is simply IT disaster recovery, or a system inventory can set recovery priority.
learningContract.formRationale: Aligned columns make concept meanings, decision criteria and failure consequences explicit and comparable.
learningContract.focalInsight: Critical function, BIA, priority, manual workaround, external dependency, communications, and remediation.
learningContract.intentionalOmissions: Do not assign a universal RTO, exercise frequency, or claim a particular supplier SLA.
learningContract.retrievalPrompt: The payment platform is intact but the call center and verification vendor are unavailable. Which function, workaround, dependency, and evidence must the exercise test?
